en.headline: Mother and relative arrested after children eat cannabis sweets
en.dek: A six-year-old boy and 12-year-old girl were taken to hospital after falling ill at their Wang Tau Hom Estate home; the mother was arrested for suspected child abuse.
body: Police arrested a mother and a relative after two children fell ill from suspected cannabis-infused sweets at their home in Wang Tau Hom Estate on Monday.

Officers received a report at about 4pm that a six-year-old boy and a 12-year-old girl had become unwell at Wang Tak House. The girl vomited repeatedly while the boy briefly lost consciousness. Both were conscious when ambulance crews took them to Queen Elizabeth Hospital for treatment.

According to police sources, the 41-year-old mother claimed she had mistaken the confectionery for ordinary sweets and given them to her children. The sweets were believed to have been brought from overseas. The mother was arrested on suspicion of child abuse or neglect, and a 61-year-old relative, described as the husband’s aunt or great-aunt, was arrested on suspicion of possessing dangerous drugs. Investigations continue.

zh.headline: 兩童誤食懷疑含大麻糖果不適 母親及親戚被捕
zh.dek: 一名六歲男童及12歲女童周一下午在橫頭磡邨家中不適送院，母親涉嫌虐待兒童被捕，另一名親戚涉嫌藏毒被捕。
body: 警方周一拘捕一名母親及一名親戚，指兩名兒童在橫頭磡邨家中疑因進食含大麻糖果而感不適。
警方約下午4時接報，橫德樓一名六歲男童及12歲女童不適。女童多次嘔吐，男童曾短暫失去知覺。救護員到場時兩童已恢復意識，並送往伊利沙伯醫院治理。
消息指，41歲母親聲稱誤將該批糖果當作普通零食給子女食用，相信糖果由海外帶回。母親涉嫌虐待或疏忽照顧兒童被捕，61歲親戚（丈夫的姑母或姑婆）則涉嫌藏有危險藥物被捕。案件仍在調查中。
